reasoning: South Carolina remains strongly Republican structurally, with a statewide Cook PVI of about R+11. The only current race-specific polling found in the last 45 days was for the Republican U.S. Senate special primary, which showed a close multi-candidate field but did not provide a general-election Senate or presidential margin for the state.

sources.name: Emerson College Polling
sources.details: Emerson College polling reported Ralph Norman at 22% and Darline Graham at 19% in the South Carolina GOP Senate special primary, indicating a close but non-general-election contest.

sources.name: The Hill
sources.details: The Hill summarized the Emerson poll, saying Norman led Graham 22% to 19% in the GOP Senate primary.

sources.name: Newsweek / Quantus Insights
sources.details: Newsweek reported a Quantus Insights poll showing Darline Graham ahead in the Republican Senate primary, 30.4% to Ralph Norman's 17.5% on the initial ballot and 33.1% to 20.4% after allocation.

sources.name: Trafalgar Group / PJ Media
sources.details: Trafalgar Group's South Carolina GOP Senate special primary tracking poll showed Darline Graham at 26.4%, ahead of Ralph Norman at 19.5% and others.

sources.name: NBC News
sources.details: NBC News published live special primary results showing Darline Graham winning the South Carolina Senate special Republican primary with 32.7% to Ralph Norman's 24.6%.
